Introduction

In a master dissertation layout, the result section is very crucial as it pay way for the dissertation discussion and dissertation conclusion . To understand the structure of a dissertation, check our dissertation guidelines study guide.
The dissertation results section, also known as the findings or analysis chapter, is one of the most Important chapters as it displays the study outcome and the analysis of the data in an easy-to-read text narrative using tables, graphs, and charts. Also, it draws attention to any potential problems that may have been discovered

Best Practice to Write a Result Section

  • The outcomes must always be expressed in the past tense it can either be Dissertation statistical analysis or textual analysis.
  • This section’s length will depend on the quantity of data gathered and examined, but it should be written as clearly as feasible.
  • Provide only the findings that are directly related to resolving the study issues. Avoid using speculative or interpretive phrases like “implies” or “appears.”
  • Always begin with the more general results and work down to the more specific (but still significant) ones.
  • Consider including any further findings in an appendix or as footnotes. The elaboration is the discussion section of a research paper.

Check our study guide on how to write a discussion chapter in a Masters dissertation for guidance on the discussion section.

Guidelines to Write Results Sections in the Master Dissertation

  • Guideline Review

    • It is crucial to check the instructions given by the instructor before writing the outcomes section of the dissertation. In addition, the guidelines will assist in deciding what should be included in the results section. The restrictions and length of the content included in the results section should be the primary concern when reading the rules. The reader’s expectations from a given part can be ascertained by reading the guidelines.

  • Think about the Research Result

    • It is a stage where focusing primarily on outcomes and discoveries connected to the study topics is essential. Therefore, it is necessary to provide subheadings when writing the results portion of the Dissertation to streamline the report; when it is used in the technique that can help the reader comprehend the investigation’s findings.

  • Create Tables and Figures for the Presentation of Information

    • The tables and figures must be numbered correctly. The information in the table should be self-explanatory. The tables should contain all necessary and pertinent information. By examining the research’s findings, the figures and tables should be presented so the reader can understand them.

  • Use figures and findings to write the results section

    • This stage’s primary goal is to show the complicated material properly. The opening paragraph of the results section should strongly emphasise connecting the investigation’s goals or research questions to the findings. The Dissertation’s outcomes section should try to be written in the past tense.

  • Revision and Editing

    • It should review the results section after it is finished because reviewing techniques will aid in finding flaws or incorrect information interpretation. To ensure that study results are presented systematically, revising, proofreading, and editing the results section is necessary. It should also validate that the research findings are accurate and relevant to the objectives, aim, and introduction.

    Conclusion

    The theme, issue, questions, and hypotheses are reiterated in the conclusion chapter. Address the key ideas from the introduction, emphasise the purpose and the methodology, and then provide a concise summary of the results and their relevance. The message will be reinforced by repeating the key elements in the discussion section. Finally, preserve the thesis’s flow and avoid including additional elements unrelated to the inquiry.
